subject: Data Engineering
title: When Lakes Become Swamps
description: A 60-second lesson on When Lakes Become Swamps.

hook.text: The lake has 50,000 files. Nobody knows what most of them contain. Welcome to the data swamp.

buildup.text: A data swamp is a lake where data is dumped without metadata, organization, or ownership.

discovery.text: Signs of a swamp: no documentation, inconsistent formats, unknown freshness, and zero access controls.

twist.text: The irony: the lake was built to make data accessible. Without governance, it made data more hidden than before.

climax.text: Preventing a swamp requires the same discipline as a warehouse: catalogs, naming conventions, and ownership.

punchline.text: A lake without governance is just an expensive swamp.

quiz.question: What turns a data lake into a data swamp?
options: Lack of metadata, organization, and ownership
